questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which term describes the maximum population size an environment can sustain indefinitely?
questions.hint: It is shown by the plateau of an S-shaped curve.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a sigmoid (logistic) growth curve, the transitional phase begins when:
options: limiting factors start to slow the growth rate
the population first colonises the habitat
questions.answer: limiting factors start to slow the growth rate
questions.hint: Resources become less available as numbers rise.

questions.q: Capture–mark–release–recapture: 40 beetles are marked and released. Later, 50 are caught, of which 8 are marked. Estimate the population size using the Lincoln index.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Only about 10% of energy is typically transferred between trophic levels mainly because:
options: energy is lost as heat from cell respiration and in undigested material
energy is destroyed at each level
consumers store all energy as fat
questions.answer: energy is lost as heat from cell respiration and in undigested material
questions.hint: Energy is not created or destroyed, but it leaves the food chain.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A species that has a disproportionately large effect on community structure relative to its abundance is a:
questions.hint: Removing it can cause the community to collapse, like an arch without its key stone.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement about natural selection is correct?
options: Individuals with heritable traits that increase survival and reproduction pass on alleles more often.
Individuals change their genes to adapt during their lifetime.
Acquired characteristics are inherited by offspring.
Selection creates new mutations when they are needed.
questions.answer: Individuals with heritable traits that increase survival and reproduction pass on alleles more often.
questions.hint: Variation must already exist and be heritable.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What type of speciation occurs when a population is divided by a geographical barrier?
questions.hint: 'Allo' means 'other'; 'patric' refers to the homeland.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Abrupt speciation in plants often occurs through:
options: geographical isolation over millions of years
questions.hint: Changes in the number of chromosome sets can isolate a new population instantly.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Differences in mating behaviour that prevent two populations from interbreeding are an example of:
questions.hint: The barrier acts before fertilisation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A clade is best defined as:
options: a common ancestor and all of its descendants
all species in the same habitat
a group of species that cannot interbreed
questions.answer: a common ancestor and all of its descendants
questions.hint: Think of one branch of a cladogram, cut off completely.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The three domains of life are:
questions.hint: Classification based mainly on rRNA sequences.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: First calculate p = 1 − q.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Calculate Simpson's reciprocal index (D = N(N−1) ÷ Σn(n−1)) for a sample with three species of 4, 3 and 3 individuals. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: N = 10. Calculate n(n−1) for each species and add them.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Outline how antibiotic resistance in bacteria provides evidence for evolution by natural selection.
questions.hint: Include variation, selection pressure, survival and reproduction, and change in allele frequency.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: Think about food supply, competition and overshoot.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss two reasons why biodiversity is currently declining and evaluate one conservation strategy (in situ or ex situ).
questions.hint: Use command terms: give strengths and limitations of the strategy.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time is a:

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which factor is density-dependent?
questions.hint: Its effect becomes stronger as the population grows.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Capture–mark–release–recapture: 30 snails are marked and released. Later, 40 are caught, of which 6 are marked. Estimate the population size using the Lincoln index.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: They form the first trophic level.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: Apply 10% twice.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement about mutualism is correct?
options: Both species benefit from the interaction.
One species benefits and the other is harmed.
One species benefits and the other is unaffected.
questions.answer: Both species benefit from the interaction.
questions.hint: Think of pollinators and flowering plants.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the best example of evidence for evolution?
options: homologous structures such as the pentadactyl limb
questions.answer: homologous structures such as the pentadactyl limb
questions.hint: Similar structures suggest common ancestry.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: For natural selection to occur, there must be:
questions.hint: Selection acts on differences that can be inherited.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the term for the formation of a new species?
questions.hint: It often follows reproductive isolation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In binomial nomenclature, the first part of a scientific name is the:
questions.hint: It is written with a capital letter.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which group is a domain of life?
questions.hint: There are three domains in total.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Cladograms are increasingly based on:
questions.hint: Molecular data act like a clock of change.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Higher biodiversity in an ecosystem is generally associated with:
questions.hint: More species can buffer disturbances.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Outline how antibiotic resistance in bacteria develops by natural selection.
questions.hint: Variation, selection by the antibiotic, survival and reproduction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why a population that grows exponentially cannot keep doing so indefinitely.
questions.hint: Think of limiting factors and carrying capacity.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Suggest two human activities that reduce biodiversity and one way to reduce the impact of each.
questions.hint: For example, habitat loss and overexploitation.

hold large buffer stocks for emergencies
buy raw materials in bulk once a year
questions.answer: minimise stock holding by receiving supplies only when needed

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the Japanese term for continuous small improvements in production?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Quality assurance differs from quality control because it:

removes the need for any standards

questions.hint: A strong recommendation weighs both sides before concluding.

questions.subject: bus

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Evaluate the use of a Boston matrix for a firm deciding which products to invest in.
questions.hint: Mention its usefulness and at least two limitations.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: How many Ps are in the traditional marketing mix for goods?
questions.hint: Product, price, promotion and…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which element of the marketing mix refers to how a product reaches customers?
questions.hint: Also called distribution.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Setting a high initial price for an innovative product is called:
questions.hint: Like removing the cream from the top of milk.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Pricing a product at $9.99 instead of $10 is an example of:
questions.hint: It plays on how customers perceive numbers.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In the product life cycle, sales grow most rapidly during the:

questions.answer: a 'buy one get one free' offer in store

questions.subject: bus

large amounts of stock are always kept
stock is ordered once a year
goods are made before customers order them

questions.hint: It reduces storage costs.

questions.q: Price per unit is $20, variable cost per unit is $12 and fixed costs are $24,000. Calculate the break-even quantity.

questions.subject: bus

questions.hint: Consider cost, reach and the target market.

questions.subject: bus

chem-sl.topic: Review: organic chemistry and reaction mechanisms
